concepts.title: Division of Labour and Cellular Hierarchy in Tissues

questions.q: What does 'division of labour' mean in multicellular organisms?
questions.a: Different cells specialise for different jobs - muscle cells contract, nerve cells carry signals - making the organism efficient.

questions.q: What is the order of organisation: cell to organism?
questions.a: Cell -> tissue -> organ -> organ system -> organism.

questions.q: Why can't a single-celled organism afford specialisation?
questions.a: One cell must do every life function itself; only many cells can share out the work.

questions.q: What is meristematic tissue?
questions.a: Plant tissue of actively dividing cells, found at growing tips, responsible for plant growth.

questions.q: Name the three kinds of meristems by position.
questions.a: Apical (tips of roots and shoots), lateral (sides, for girth) and intercalary (at nodes/bases of leaves).

questions.q: Why do meristem cells have thin walls and dense cytoplasm?
questions.a: They are busy dividing; thin walls ease division and dense cytoplasm supports rapid growth with no storage vacuoles.

questions.q: Name the three simple permanent tissues of plants.
questions.a: Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma.

questions.q: Which simple tissue gives flexible support to leaf stalks?
questions.a: Collenchyma - living cells with thickened corners that bend without breaking.

questions.q: What makes sclerenchyma stiff and dead at maturity?
questions.a: Its cell walls are thickened with lignin; the dead hard cells give mechanical strength.

concepts.title: Complex Permanent Tissues and Vascular Systems

questions.q: Name the two complex permanent tissues of plants.
questions.a: Xylem and phloem.

questions.q: Why are xylem and phloem called complex tissues?
questions.a: Each is made of more than one type of cell working together as a transport unit.

questions.q: What do xylem and phloem transport?
questions.a: Xylem carries water and minerals upward from roots; phloem carries food from leaves to other parts.

questions.q: What is epithelial tissue and where is it found?
questions.a: A sheet of tightly packed cells covering body surfaces and lining cavities and organs.

questions.q: Name two jobs of epithelial tissue.
questions.a: Protection against injury and germs, and secretion/absorption (as in gland and gut linings).

questions.q: How are epithelial cells suited to their job?
questions.a: They fit closely with almost no cementing material between them, forming continuous sheets.

questions.q: What are the parts of connective tissue?
questions.a: Scattered cells embedded in an abundant matrix, which may be solid, jelly-like or fluid.

questions.q: Name three types of connective tissue with one example each.
questions.a: Loose connective (areolar under skin), dense (tendons, ligaments), and specialised (bone, cartilage, blood).

questions.q: Why is blood called a connective tissue?
questions.a: It has cells (RBC, WBC, platelets) in a fluid plasma matrix and connects body parts by transport.

concepts.title: Muscular Tissues - Skeletal, Smooth, and Cardiac

questions.q: Name the three kinds of muscle tissue.
questions.a: Skeletal (voluntary, striped), smooth (involuntary, unstriated) and cardiac (heart) muscle.

questions.q: Which muscle type works without our will and is found in the gut?
questions.a: Smooth (unstriated) muscle moves food along the gut involuntarily.

questions.q: What is special about cardiac muscle?
questions.a: It is involuntary, striped, with branched fibres, and never tires - it beats throughout life.

concepts.title: Structure and Function of Nervous Tissue and Neurons

questions.q: Name the parts of a neuron.
questions.a: Cell body (cyton), dendrites, axon and axon terminals.

questions.q: Which part of a neuron receives signals and which sends them onward?
questions.a: Dendrites receive information; the axon carries it away to the nerve endings.

questions.q: Why can a nerve impulse travel so fast?
questions.a: The signal is electrical along the axon, and chemical transfer occurs only at the tiny synapse gaps.

concepts.title: Joint Types in the Musculoskeletal System

questions.q: Name the four main types of joints in the human body.
questions.a: Ball and socket, hinge, pivot and fixed (immovable) joints.

questions.q: Which joint lets the arm rotate in all directions?
questions.a: The ball-and-socket joint of the shoulder (and hip).

questions.q: Where are fixed joints found?
questions.a: In the skull - the bony plates meet at immovable joints that protect the brain.

concepts.title: Estimation of Tree Age from Annual Growth Rings

questions.q: How can the age of a tree be estimated?
questions.a: By counting the annual rings (growth rings) seen in a cross-section of its trunk.

questions.q: What causes annual rings to form?
questions.a: Wood grows at different speeds in different seasons, making alternating light and dark rings each year.

questions.q: Does the trunk diameter grow evenly through the year?
questions.a: No - growth is more in favourable seasons and less in unfavourable ones, giving ring boundaries.
